correctness.rationale: A sixteen-word domination lower bound is attained by the Hamming code, and equality forces a partition into eight-vertex closed neighborhoods. Translating one selected word to zero forces a Steiner triple system from the 21 weight-two words; the remaining 28 weight-three words force all seven line-complements, and the seven weight-six words force all ones. The 30 labeled Fano-plane systems and eight cosets of each exhaust all 240 minima. Two independent integer implementations respectively use triple exact cover and parity-check-column permutation, verify every efficient code and all 28680 unordered intersections, reconstruct all 1680 eight-exchange edges, and breadth-first traverse from all 240 starts with constant sphere profile (1,14,63,106,56); this gives connectedness, triangle freeness, degree14, and diameter4. Certificate and replay outputs are packaged. Finite computation claims only this finite graph.

value.rationale: Minimum domination of hypercubes is a standard natural extremal graph problem with perfect-code configurations. Here the complete optimum set has a counterintuitive mobility threshold: no replacement of seven or fewer guards can preserve minimum domination, but replacing eight permits a connected 240-state vertex-transitive triangle-free graph with sharp diameter four. Determining all pairwise shortest-path spheres and the exact local degree distinguishes substantially different reconfiguration behavior beyond repeating the known optimum or enumerating a random subset. It is a complete, motivated finite geometry result; there is no claim of downstream theorem or unlimited extension.
